brief.headline: Ghana's EU Timber Licence Path and a $650M North American Coffee Sale
brief.dek: A look at how Ghana's EU timber partnership reshaped forest governance, plus Kraft Heinz agrees to sell its North American coffee business.
brief.lede: Ghana's long-running timber legality partnership with the EU is drawing attention as a model for building forest governance. It is a relevant reference point for wood exporters facing EU legality and due-diligence demands.

sections.heading: Ghana's timber deal with the EU
bullets: Ghana spent 16 years on its Voluntary Partnership Agreement process with the EU before reaching a milestone last year.
The deal offered EU market access plus support to strengthen national forest governance, giving exporters a clearer legality framework.
Europe is a key buyer of Ghanaian timber, so shifting EU legality expectations directly affect the country's wood trade.
A Mongabay analysis argues the new licence has improved institutions and cooperation in the sector.

sections.heading: Kraft Heinz exits North American coffee
bullets: Kraft Heinz agreed to sell its North American coffee business to One Rock for $650 million.
The company will keep a 30% stake and use the cash to pay down debt.
Coffee suppliers and traders should watch for any changes in sourcing relationships under new majority ownership.
